subject: Retention: default capture (requests & outputs), export ownership and deletion workflow
messages:
From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@finbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finbridge.com, legal@finbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs) + export/delete process

Hi Jordan,

Quick follow-up from our security review: we need a plain-language summary of Redwood's default capture policy for hosted API usage. Specifically:

- What is retained by default for a typical request? (raw user input, intermediate tokens, final output)
- How long is each element retained in hosted vs dedicated/private deployments?
- If we request an export of our data, who "owns" that export? And after export, what are our options to have the copies removed from Redwood systems (and which systems)?

Can you also point us to the ticket/runbook we should use to initiate a deletion or export? I'm attaching a short list of FinBridge's compliance needs.

Thanks,
Ethan

Attachment: finbridge_retention_questions.pdf (PDF stub, 42KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@finbridge.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@finbridge.com, legal@finbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs) + export/delete process

Hi Ethan — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR up top, then details and next steps below.

TL;DR:
- Hosted API default: we store request inputs and final outputs for 30 days for operational telemetry; derivative telemetry (latency/aggregate metrics) is stored longer per our analytics retention. Streamed token buffers (KV cache) are ephemeral and not stored beyond the request lifecycle unless a customer opts into session recording.
- Dedicated/Private: default behavior is configurable by contract; many enterprise customers set hosted-like defaults or elect to disable persistence entirely.
- Exports: when we create an export for a customer, the exported file is owned by the customer. Redwood maintains a short-term copy (48–72 hours) in an internal transfer store to allow download; after successful transfer we delete those copies unless retention is requested in writing.

Details:
1) What we keep by default (hosted API):
   - User-provided prompt/request text: retained for 30 days to support debugging/abuse investigations and to power quality alerts.
   - Final model outputs (the generated text or structured response): retained for 30 days.
   - Per-request metadata (latency, model version, route): retained as aggregated telemetry for 180 days; raw request identifiers are removed after 30 days unless part of an incident investigation.
   - Streamed tokens / KV cache: transient only — not written to durable storage unless session recording is enabled by the customer.

2) Dedicated and Private:
   - For Dedicated (reserved capacity) we ship a default policy that mirrors hosted, but customers can contractually require shorter/longer windows or disable storage; those controls are set at provisioning time.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem) — Redwood's control plane can be configured to not persist requests; policy is controlled by the customer and detailed in the deployment playbook.

3) Exports & ownership:
   - Any export we produce (S3/CSV/NDJSON) is generated on request and is considered customer property. Redwood stores the export in an internal transfer area for up to 72 hours to allow secure handoff. After the customer confirms receipt we schedule automatic deletion of the internal copy.
   - If a signed agreement requires longer internal retention for audit purposes, that must be documented in the contract.

4) Deletion workflow (how FinBridge requests erasure):
   - Create a support ticket at https://support.redwood.ai with the account id and export_manifest id (we'll provide a sample manifest).
   - For hosted customers: deletion of request/response artifacts is processed within 30 days from approval; exports are removed from the transfer area within 72 hours after confirmation of receipt.
   - For Dedicated/Private: deletion timing is governed by the environment; for Private on-prem we provide runbooks to delete local artifacts.

Next steps: I attached an export manifest example that shows the IDs we need to process an export/delete. Kimberly, can you confirm the deletion SLA language for hosted exports and supply the exact support-runbook link? Marissa, looping you in for any commercial notes on adding explicit export retention terms to the SOW.

-- Jordan

Attachment: export_manifest_example.csv (CSV stub, 1KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@finbridge.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@finbridge.com, legal@finbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs) + export/delete process

Thanks Jordan — adding a couple clarifications from compliance:

- The 30-day default is specifically for the "request/response artifact store" on hosted. We retain aggregated metrics (no PII) for 180 days.
- For deletion: we require a ticket plus an authorized requestor (list of emails or signed request from a company admin). For legal holds / litigation we place a temporary hold and communicate timelines; normal deletion requests are processed after hold checks complete.
- Cross-region deletion: if you have data in multiple regions, our deletion job will target all region-local stores but will require the manifest listing the region-scoped dataset ids.

I've dropped the support article link here: https://support.redwood.ai/articles/data-export-and-deletion (internal + customer-facing). Jordan: the hosted export internal retention is 48–72 hours by default; we remove the transfer copy automatically after a successful download or after 72 hours.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@finbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@finbridge.com, legal@finbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs) + export/delete process

Jordan / Kimberly — this is helpful, thank you. A few quick follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm the default retention in writing (we will include the clause in our vendor binder)? If possible we prefer a written statement with the 30-day/72-hour numbers.
2) For exports: if we request an export and then ask Redwood to delete any internal transfer copies immediately (without waiting for our confirmation), can you support that? We want the option to avoid a transfer copy living in any intermediate store.
3) For session recordings: how does an admin opt-out globally?

If you can respond with short bullets we can close the item on our end.

Thanks,
Ethan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Liu <ethan.liu@finbridge.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security@finbridge.com, legal@finbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs) + export/delete process

Ethan — short bullets below. I'm copying the support article link and will attach a signed statement if you'd like one for your vendor binder.

1) Written confirmation (official): Hosted default retention: prompts/requests retained for 30 days; final outputs retained for 30 days; internal transfer copies for exports retained up to 72 hours. Aggregated telemetry retained for 180 days. We can provide a signed PDF with these numbers if you need it in the binder.

2) Immediate-delete export option: yes — we support a "no-transfer" export mode for customers who require it. Two caveats: (a) the export may take longer to prepare (we avoid creating a durable transfer copy), and (b) we require a customer admin to confirm receipt (or sign an acceptance) so we can close the job without a transfer artifact. We will document this option in the export runbook.

3) Session recording opt-out: Admins can disable session recording at the account level in the Console (Console > Account settings > Session recording = OFF). For Dedicated/Private, this is a field in the provisioning/manifest and can be set to false at deploy time.

Action items:
- Jordan: provide signed short retention statement for FinBridge (by end of day tomorrow).
- Kimberly: confirm the support article is public-facing and share link for vendor binder.
- Marissa: flag for SOW language if FinBridge wants the no-transfer export mode as a contractual option.

Thanks — Jordan

--
